continuous_text.title: Let's Dress Up!
continuous_text.content:
Let's dress up!
Come on! Come on!
Let's dress up!
Let's play!
[Repeat]

Those socks are long.
That hat is blue.
That T-shirt is old,
And it's colorful, too.
continuous_text.notes: Audio tracks 143 and 144. Includes alternative adjective substitution cues: short, cap, jacket, beautiful.

continuous_text.title: The Shoemaker
continuous_text.content:
Frame 1
Narrator: This is the shoemaker.
Shoemaker: Oh, no! There are a lot of shoes!

Frame 2
Narrator: These are the mice.
Narrator: She's tired!
Mice: Poor shoemaker!

Frame 3
Narrator: The mice can make shoes, too.
Mice: Let's help the shoemaker!

Frame 4
Narrator: The shoemaker is happy.
Shoemaker: These shoes are fantastic!

Frame 5
Customer Woman: Those shoes are beautiful!
Customer Man: I want those shoes, please.

Frame 6
Narrator: But who are the shoemakers?
Shoemaker: Two little mice!
Customer Woman: His T-shirt is old. Her jacket is old. Poor mice!

Frame 7
Narrator: The shoemaker has an idea.
Shoemaker: These are his pants. This is her skirt.

Frame 8
Boy Mouse: Look! New clothes!
Mice: Hurray!
continuous_text.speaker_structure: Narrator, Shoemaker, Mice, Customer Woman, Customer Man, Boy Mouse
continuous_text.notes: Lesson 4 Story spanning pages 90 and 91. Adaptation of 'The Elves and the Shoemaker' highlighting helpfulness and gratitude.

continuous_text.title: Clothes in My Country
continuous_text.content:
I'm Callum. I'm from Scotland in the U.K. These are clothes from my country.
I have a kilt. A kilt is a skirt. I have a blue shirt, a black hat, and a black jacket, too. My jacket is new. It's long!
This is my sister, Becky. These are her favorite clothes. She has a black hat, black socks, and black shoes. She has a kilt, too. Her kilt is colorful.
What are your favorite clothes?
continuous_text.notes: Lesson 5 Reading passage formatted as a classroom blog post.
